Verizon Innovation Center, Boston

Gensler · 2022 · For Verizon

Built across three floors of Verizon’s new Boston headquarters, the center is where enterprise customers explore Verizon’s solutions and work with its experts to test their own ideas.

Visitors are greeted by an elevator lobby welcome moment, then embark on a journey built around them. Modular kiosk carts tell different demo stories, a portable immersive AR room transports visitors to Verizon labs in other cities, and transformable workshop spaces host hands-on sessions. A flip screen wall frames conversations with customers about their industry. Two immersive theaters accented with dynamic digital sculptures tell the bigger stories, and one hides a secret portal.

Donald Richardson · Selected work

GSync

Gensler · Self-started

Digital experience projects vary in scope, scale, technology, teams and vendors. These differences mean that projects are mostly one-offs, built from scratch every time. The result is duplicated effort, missed efficiencies and a growing maintenance burden.

So I built GSync, a shared platform for content management, distribution and infrastructure, designed to be reused across projects while allowing each experience to remain unique.

What it was

  • Schema-driven content models and CMS
  • A shared GraphQL content layer
  • Content distribution, sync and scheduling
  • Change notifications and event forwarding
  • Client adapters for web, TouchDesigner and more

How it was built

  • Funded by client projects
  • Improved iteratively with each project
  • Its proven success led to its adoption as a standard for projects across Gensler studios

Donald Richardson · Selected work

The Platform

Gensler · Platform Technology Director

GSync’s track record led the firm to form a platform technology group around it, which I co-led. The goal was to make digital experiences turnkey, cheaper to deliver, hardened and easier to maintain.

Cloud

  • Self-hosted on AWS, provisioned with Pulumi
  • Multi-tenant Webiny CMS with access governance across clients
  • Event-driven, with RabbitMQ carrying jobs and events to each site
  • Containerized workers for video transcoding and image processing

On site

  • Reusable client applications as a standard foundation
  • Packaged Electron apps as an admin interface for clients
  • Local logging, metrics, alerts and dashboards at each site

Delivery and operations

  • Central observability across sites with ELK, Prometheus and Grafana
  • Client apps built in CI, stored in an artifact repository
  • Feature flags for real automated updates
  • Planned: continuous deployment to test environments

Part two

A sample pilot

A discovery readout for Aurora, a fictional consumer audio brand. A way to show my thinking and start a conversation, not a proposal.

What we heard in discovery

Simulated findings

Interviews with marketing, the in-house studio, martech and legal.

The pain point

Each launch needs hundreds of product images across channels and markets. The studio builds them by hand, so launches wait on production.

Their stack

  • Creative Cloud and AEM Assets
  • Workfront for requests and approvals
  • CAD from product engineering
  • Product data in a PIM

Their guardrails

  • Legal approves all generated imagery
  • Indemnified models only
  • Product shape, color and logo must be exact

Aurora pilot · a fictional example

The future state

People focus on

Art direction, campaign ideas, and judging what’s on brand.

The system handles

Packshots, scene variants, resizing, copy versions, and keeping a record of how every image was made.

3D product master, from CAD

Scenes generated with Firefly

Product composited, templates filled

Review, then AEM Assets

What we build

  • A 3D master and packshots from CAD
  • Three scene templates, two formats, two markets
  • Scenes from an indemnified model, product composited in
  • Review with the studio lead and legal

How we judge it

  • Turnaround, brief to approved
  • Cost per image, against today’s baseline
  • Approval rounds and product accuracy
  • How the studio team feels about it

Out of scope for the pilot: video, AR and more markets · Hosted in our environment

Adoption, audience by audience

Planned with ADKAR: awareness, desire, knowledge, ability and reinforcement, worked out for each group.

AudienceWhat gets them there
Studio designersHands-on training, a champion on the team, and seeing their judgment kept at the center
MarketingFaster turnaround they can see, and a simple way to request work
LegalClear rules on which models are used, review steps, and a record for every image
Martech and ITA fit with their stack and an early security review
